classification.difficultyReason: Use a reverse bearing, cosine-rule distance and sine-rule angle to obtain the return bearing.

content.prompt: A ship sails 50 km from port $A$ to port $B$ on a bearing of $063^\circ\mathrm{T}$, then sails 130 km from port $B$ to port $C$ on a bearing of $296^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14, lower-left diagram below parts a–c
spec.description: Black triangle ABC with A lowest, B upper-right and C upper-left. Dashed unlabelled north arrows rise from all three vertices. Includes 63-degree bearing arc at A, reflex 296-degree arc at B, a separate unlabelled interior arc at B, 130 km on BC, and a 50 km label below AB with a curved pointer to its midpoint. No point D.
spec.mathematics: AB=50 km on bearing 063 degrees; BC=130 km on bearing 296 degrees. Uniform scale 0.04 cm per km. Interior angle ABC is the anticlockwise sector from BC to BA.

answer.worked:
Extend the north line at $B$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }B &= 63^\circ+180^\circ\\&=243^\circ\\\angle ABC &= 296^\circ-243^\circ\\&=53^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find, correct to the nearest km the distance of port $A$ from port $C$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find $\angle ACB$, and hence find the bearing of port $A$ from port $C$, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\angle ACB}{50} &= \frac{\sin53^\circ}{AC}\\\sin\angle ACB &= \frac{50\sin53^\circ}{\sqrt{50^2+130^2-2(50)(130)\cos53^\circ}}\\\angle ACB &= \sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{50\sin53^\circ}{\sqrt{50^2+130^2-2(50)(130)\cos53^\circ}}\right)\\&\approx22^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\angle ACB$ is acute because it is opposite the shortest side. Using the unrounded angle,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }B\text{ from }C &= 296^\circ-180^\circ\\&=116^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C &= 116^\circ+\angle ACB\\&\approx138^\circ\end{align*}$$
